general.temas: Recurring topics include the upcoming APEC summit and the planned meeting of the leaders of Russia, the United States and China, as well as the war in Ukraine and its consequences, including the attack on the Crimean Bridge. Several outlets cover economic issues and the plane crash in Kemerovo. Only Meduza highlights the conviction in absentia of journalist Andrei Soldatov.
general.motivo_crispacion: Tensions stem mainly from the war between Russia and Ukraine, the attack on the Crimean Bridge and the operations the FSB attributes to Ukrainian intelligence services. Warnings about possible European military involvement and political differences in Italy over aid to Kyiv also feature prominently. In Russia, the conviction of a journalist and cases against donors add to institutional and social conflict. News about the diplomatic summit, the economy, culture and tourism partly offsets this picture.

Kommersant.resumen:
- NATO will fund a mechanism to give its military satellites access to commercial rockets; the front page also covers a proposed new US nuclear bomb.
- The APEC summit in Shenzhen will bring together the leaders of China, Russia and the United States.
- The front page reports on the review of footballer Matvei Safonov's alimony case and the reduction of fighter Usman Nurmagomedov's sentence.
- Damage to the Crimean Bridge could worsen the decline in tourism; the FSB says it has thwarted drone attacks in southern Russia.
- The cost of transporting Russian oil to India and China is falling; a Russian court orders a US company to pay a debt for crab supplies.
Kommersant.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly factual, although phrases such as “Israel scares the United States with Iran” and a reference to an urgent situation in space add drama.
Kommersant.sesgo: The selection gives weight to security and the economic repercussions for Russia. The headline about Israel presents the exchange of intelligence as an attempt to scare the United States.

Rossíiskaya Gazeta.resumen:
- DOM.RF opens applications for preferential financing for urban projects in the Far East.
- France confirms the presence of a French military structure in Ukraine.
- The governor of Kuzbass reports on a plane crash and publishes images of the site.
- Experts examine trends in new-home prices amid falling demand.
- The front page also covers rural tourism, an artistic exchange with Beijing, the weather, travel from Sevastopol and judicial and educational issues.
Rossíiskaya Gazeta.motivo_populismo: The headlines are mostly factual; phrases such as “strengthened legal protection” add some emphasis, without resorting to disparagement or confrontation between groups.
Rossíiskaya Gazeta.sesgo: The selection gives prominence to institutional initiatives, authorities and Russian regional issues, with a practical focus on housing, services and education. The news is presented mainly through official and expert sources.

Komsomólskaya Pravda.resumen:
- The number of layoffs in Russia fell to its lowest level in six years.
- The front page covers the upcoming meeting of Putin, Trump and Xi in Shenzhen and a proposal by the Italian opposition related to aid for Ukraine.
- An expert warns of a scam involving purported Children's Day payments.
- In Moscow and its surrounding areas, Panfilov's men were commemorated on the 85th anniversary of their feat.
- The front page also includes news about social initiatives, family films and the lives of several artists.
Komsomólskaya Pravda.motivo_populismo: Emotive expressions such as “immortal feat,” alarmist language about scams and disparaging phrases such as “the so-called European leaders” appear, although several headlines are factual.
Komsomólskaya Pravda.sesgo: The selection combines political and social issues with entertainment. Russian patriotic framing and the inclusion of voices critical of European leaders stand out in the political and commemorative coverage.

Védomosti.resumen:
- Lavrov and Ryabkov discussed negotiations on Ukraine and the planned meeting of the leaders of Russia, the United States and China.
- A drone attack damaged structures on the Crimean Bridge; the FSB reported an operation against alleged Ukrainian attack plans in southern Russia.
- The Duma approved on first reading a bill to promote the image of families with three or more children in advertising.
- A health official said that 5.6% of births in Russia in 2025 were premature; technological cooperation between Russia and Africa also features prominently.
- Economic coverage includes changes at Cosmos Hotel Group, increased tipping in retail, a revenue growth forecast for MTS and declines on the Russian stock market.
Védomosti.motivo_populismo: The headlines are mostly factual; evaluative phrases such as “one of the best results in the world” and “a politician of turbulent times” add some intensity, but there is no disparagement or appeal to the people against the elites.
Védomosti.sesgo: The selection on diplomacy and security relies mainly on statements from Russian officials, with no other perspectives appearing in the texts provided. Issues presented in a positive light for Russia, such as the birth rate and cooperation with Africa, also feature prominently.

Meduza.resumen:
- Robert Pattinson will be the new James Bond.
- A military plane crashed in Kemerovo; preliminary reports say everyone on board was killed.
- Estonia's president calls for an assessment of the consequences of closing the border with Russia; accounts from people living under bombardment are included.
- The Duma is considering raising the maximum age for women's military service and a special bankruptcy regime for participants in the war.
- The front page reports on the conviction of a journalist, cases against donors to political prisoners and a business position for Putin's son-in-law.
Meduza.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly factual, although emotional devices appear in the accounts of people under bombardment, along with a provocative question in the hackers' message: “Were you afraid to confront Russia?”
Meduza.sesgo: The selection pays particular attention to the war, its consequences and the actions of the Russian authorities, including reports on convictions and Putin's family connections. It also includes international, cultural and sporting topics.

opiniones.comunista:
Today I see a contest over priorities. NATO is preparing military access to commercial rockets, while a US Senate committee has included funding for a new nuclear bomb in a budget bill. The alliance between public power and big capital finds resources when it comes to militarization; I would like to see the same determination to guarantee housing, healthcare and education.

In Russia, financing has been announced for urban projects in the Far East, and news reports record a slowdown in the growth of new-home prices. But building more or slowing price rises is not enough if access continues to depend on private profitability. I advocate public housing and collective ownership, with democratic control by those who work and live in those areas.

Negotiations between powers must seek peace, not divide up spheres of influence. The working class needs security and rights, not another arms race.
opiniones.anarquista:
Today I see a contradiction that crosses borders: while NATO prepares access to commercial rockets for its military satellites, the United States is planning to fund a new nuclear bomb. Governments call the concentration of instruments of destruction security; I distrust a security built without the control of those who would suffer its consequences.

I am also concerned that cases have been opened in Russia against people who donated to a campaign supporting political prisoners. Solidarity should not be subject to authorization by those in power. In the face of states and parties that seek to decide for us, I advocate mutual aid networks and self-managed communities: spaces where we cooperate without bosses, protect individual freedom and make collective decisions on matters that affect everyone.
opiniones.liberal:
I worry that economic policy confuses development with the distribution of preferential financing. The new financing for projects in the Far East may benefit particular initiatives, but I prefer equal rules for everyone, low taxes and legal certainty: entrepreneurs and their customers, not official plans, are best placed to discover what deserves to prosper.

That is why I welcome the Supreme Court's clarification of protections for the owners of old country houses. Secure property rights make it possible to invest and plan without fear of arbitrary decisions. And the conviction in absentia of a journalist for spreading allegedly false information about the army reminds me that economic freedom is not enough: freedom of expression must also be protected. I want a limited state that guarantees rights, not one that makes decisions for us or punishes criticism. Freedom demands, in return, that we take responsibility for what we choose.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
The attack on the Crimean Bridge is a reminder that sovereignty is defended not with declarations, but by protecting infrastructure and ensuring that people can travel and return home. NATO, for its part, is preparing faster access to commercial rockets for its military satellites. I would not entrust Russian security to the goodwill of an alliance that is strengthening its capabilities.

The planned meeting between Russia, China and the United States may open up opportunities, but no great power should decide for us. I distrust both the elites' enthusiasm for summits and headlines promising a new era: I will judge the results by their usefulness to the country.

I also welcome the debate about the image of large families. But honoring the family requires more than advertising: it requires conditions in which children can be raised in safety and dignity.
opiniones.centro:
The upcoming meeting of the leaders of Russia, the United States and China may open up a diplomatic opportunity, but I would distrust any agreement on Ukraine that does not include the participation of Ukrainians themselves. Lasting peace requires negotiation, verifiable guarantees and respect for international institutions, not merely understandings between great powers.

I am also concerned about the conviction in absentia of journalist Andrei Soldatov for alleged falsehoods about the Russian army. A secure society needs a free press and courts capable of protecting it, even when its reporting makes those in power uncomfortable.

On the economic front, the financing program for projects in the Far East could attract investment and improve services. But public money must be allocated transparently and assessed by the results it delivers for the population. I prefer gradual, accountable reforms to grand promises without accountability.
